subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a pixel art koala clinging to a eucalyptus trunk with a branch stand, aiming for a compact but visually rich design using blocky fur textures and a sitting pose hugging the vertical trunk.

I'll reorient the branch to run along z instead, with the koala sitting facing forward, hands gripping the branch ahead and feet behind, post at the back and leaves hanging from the branch tip and post top. For the build itself, I'll keep it bounded by using a minimal rigged skeleton with hips, spine, head, jaw, arms, legs, and ears as basic joint-based parts.

Mapping out joint positions...

Still positioning limbs...

I'm setting up a named joint chain for the rig (shoulder, elbow, hand per side) parented appropriately to the chest and hips, then planning the fur paint as a cell-shaded gradient driven by noise and vertical position, with a lighter tone for the belly.

For the torso I'm deciding between a smooth sweep with varying radii versus a blockier box-based sweep to keep the koala's pixel-art feel, using cellPaint for shading either way, and starting the spine chain path at the hips.

I'm laying out the spine chain with three joints (spine1, spine2, chest), then attaching the head to the chest tip using absolute model-space coordinates rather than local bone-relative directions to avoid orientation issues, with the hips acting as the root joint.

Now I'm planning the torso and branch geometry: a tapered sweep for the body with a rump sphere, and non-rigged branch parts bound to the hips joint so they stay fixed. For foliage, I'm setting up leaf cards using lanceolate blue-green leaf SVGs placed on frames along twig sweeps, generating roughly 30 leaf frames oriented outward from the branch tips.

I'm also planning the texture set — leaf SVG, pixel-art eyes, nose highlight, ear inner shading, bark paint, and a small plaque with text — then figuring out where to place the pixel-art eye planes on the front of the head box based on its dimensions.

Switching the head to a low-poly sphere instead of a box for a rounder koala shape, I'm calculating where the eyes sit on the curved surface using the sphere's radius, then opting to use decals to place the eye textures directly onto the head geometry rather than separate planes.

For the nose, I'm adding a small protruding box shape positioned front and center, wider than tall for that oval koala nose look, with a possible nostril decal on its front face. For the mouth I'm placing a small jaw box below it with a cream chin color.

Now thinking through the ears -- flattened spheres positioned on either side with smaller cream inner discs set slightly forward, plus scattered fur tuft cards around the rims for a fluffy texture. For the hands, I'm planning small boxes with three dark claw shapes attached, positioned to grip around the branch.

Working out the arm joints -- shoulder, elbow, and hand positions on each side -- then placing three finger boxes wrapping the branch at slightly staggered depths to suggest a gripping pose. Now starting on the leg placement with the hips positioned at the sides.

Defining the torso sweep shape with a pear-like radius profile along the spine chain, then setting up a cream belly paint region based on normal and position thresholds, and starting a grey fur ramp for shading.

Now I'm adding noise-based variation to the fur tone and lighter cheek highlighting, then building the wooden base: an octagonal disc with plank-style wood coloring and a post extending upward to support an angled branch stand.

Sweeping the branch path forward from the post and adding a taller rising trunk behind the koala for leaf attachments, with forked twigs branching off at different heights and angles to hold foliage, plus a shorter forward branch near the koala's resting height.

I'm also adding a small vertical support peg under the floating branch tip to ground it, defining the base wood coloring and floor thickness, and sketching a lanceolate leaf texture in SVG with a darker shaded half and a vein line, scattered randomly across the branches as small leaf cards.

Now I'm scattering leaf surfaces along the twig sweeps, filtering out ones too near the trunk base, with around 18 per twig group plus the tip. I'm also placing a small gold-on-dark "KOALA" text plaque on the top front edge of the base, angled so it reads clearly when viewed from the front.

I'm sorting out positions so the plaque and peg don't collide, computing the base radius at a given z to keep the plaque width within bounds, and planning blocky pixel-style ears using scaled low-segment spheres with flat shading via a reusable ball helper that sets non-uniform scale on the sphere geometry.

Now I'm designing small pixel-art textures for the eyes and nose as decals — a rounded dark-and-white pattern for the eyes and a shaded dark pattern with a highlight pixel for the nose, applied onto flat box parts.

For the ears, I'm adding cream-colored inner spheres and scattering small fur-tuft cards across both ear surfaces with slight random positioning and tinted coloring. I'm also scattering cream fur cards across the chest/torso area, filtered to only appear on forward-facing surfaces.

Now I'm defining the skeleton structure: setting up the head joint attached to the spine tip with its own orientation, adding a jaw joint parented to the head, and starting to build the arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and hand joints connected back to the torso.

Pulling in the paint helper from the pixel kit and the noise function from the SDK core.
